angle_name: Conductor-lowered signed dispersion for the prime–Möbius hyperbola
mechanism: Define η(n)=1_{n prime}−(Li(n)−Li(n−1)), so R(N)=Σ_{n≤N}η(n) up to a fixed endpoint convention. On the canonical window K=y is fixed and S(y,X)=Σ_{dn≤X,d≤y}μ(d)η(n). Smooth only the hyperbola boundary at scale W≈√x, expand the windowed second moment, and apply a δ/Jutila decomposition to dn−em while retaining the complete μ(d)μ(e)η(n)η(m) sum. The averaging lowers the relevant circle-method conductor to q≈√(x/W)=x^{1/4}. Treat large-q and nonzero-shift packets using bilinear Kloosterman large-sieve estimates after exact Vaughan decomposition of the prime weight and an exact finite Möbius identity. The decisive step is to evaluate the entire low-q major-arc packet, including q=1, before any Cauchy–Schwarz or dyadic absolute-value recombination; cancellation between d-scales must remain visible. Prime-power corrections from Λ/log are retained as separate signed sparse packets rather than discarded absolutely.
new_leverage: The kernel-backed canonical-window theorem supplies exactly the Fejér-type averaging needed for conductor lowering. This replaces the killed bounded-fiber transfer by spectral averaging over all fibers and uses moduli q≲x^{1/4}, not the astronomical wheel modulus. More importantly, the proposed low-major-arc calculation keeps μ and the centered prime discrepancy in one packet, so it is outside the proved F-closure and its zero-coordinate shadow. The q=1 packet is explicitly recognized as the make-or-break signed term rather than hidden behind generic dispersion.

target_estimate.name: Signed Low-Conductor Hyperbola Packet Bound
target_estimate.statement: Let K_W(u,v;x0)=Σ_{0≤t<W}1_{u≤x0−t}1_{v≤x0−t}. Prove, after the δ-decomposition with Q=x^{1/4+o(1)}, that the combined low-conductor contribution q≤Q to Σ_{d,e≤y}Σ_{n,m≥2} μ(d)μ(e)η(n)η(m)K_W(dn,em;x0) is ≪ε W x^{1+ε}; the complementary conductor, diagonal, boundary, and prime-power packets should satisfy the same bound by existing bilinear and divisor-moment estimates. Crucially, the assertion is for the sum over all d-scales and all low q, not separately for each dyadic block.

obstacle_positions.1: No Mertens-energy input and no separation of the two factors: Cauchy–Schwarz is postponed until after the complete signed low-q packet has been evaluated.
obstacle_positions.2: Growing pair-to-modulus fibers are accepted; the δ-method and spectral large sieve estimate their total L2 multiplicity instead of demanding bounded fibers.
obstacle_positions.3: The argument is built specifically for the backward window at x0=(y+1)^2−1, using its fixed K and the sanctioned mean-square-to-pin transfer.
obstacle_positions.4: Only conductor-lowered moduli q≲x^{1/4+o(1)} occur; no estimate depends on the full wheel modulus.
obstacle_positions.5: Parity is not bypassed by a sieve majorant: μ remains a signed coefficient through the major-arc evaluation, while Vaughan identities are used as exact identities.
obstacle_positions.6: No pointwise bound for R and no absolute sum over zeros is assumed; any off-line zero must manifest as failure of the joint q=1 packet estimate.
obstacle_positions.7: Finite computations are used only for the kill test and parameter calibration, never as evidence for the estimate.
obstacle_positions.8: Wigert jumps enter the exact quadratic form; their diagonal contribution is controlled by averaged divisor moments, with no pointwise polylogarithmic smoothness claim.
obstacle_positions.9: There is no renewal induction or scalar telescope. Heath-Brown/Vaughan decompositions serve only as support-tracked finite coefficient identities inside dispersion.

kill_test: Isolate the q=1 major arc before doing any long calculation. Perform every proposed coefficient identity symbolically and check whether the resulting bound still requires estimating Σ_{d≤y}μ(d)R(x/d) blockwise, |M(y)|, or |R(x/d)|. If it does, or if replacing μ by arbitrary |a_d|≤1 leaves the proof unchanged, the route has lost the required signed interaction and should be killed immediately. A secondary exponent ledger at D≈N≈√x should verify that the best available Kloosterman large-sieve bound actually beats x^2 for the windowed moment.
rung1_version: Prove the same combined packet estimate with W x^{2−2δ} in place of W x^{1+ε} for one explicit δ>0, initially δ=1/100. Together with matching bounds for the complementary packets, this gives the unconditional fixed saving S≪x^{1−δ+ε}.
plausible_partial: Give an exact, endpoint-correct reduction from the Abel windowed moment to the four-variable kernel above; separate and bound its diagonal and prime-power packets; execute conductor lowering; and prove that all remaining difficulty is confined to an explicitly written low-q signed major-arc packet containing q=1. The discrete reduction and support statements are good candidates for Lean formalization.
weakest_assumption: A uniform power-saving estimate for the complete signed low-conductor packet, including q=1, with μ and the centered prime weight kept coupled across all d-scales. No zero-free strip, RH, pointwise prime-error estimate, or bounded-fiber assertion is assumed.
